change.requirement_text:
# Requirement #2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

requirement_points.text: For a [MessagePackObject] type in the compiling assembly that has a member whose type is a closed generic value type declared in a referenced assembly, the source generator completes without throwing IndexOutOfRangeException and does not emit CS8785.
For the same scenario, the MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer completes without throwing IndexOutOfRangeException and does not emit AD0001.
The compiling assembly receives a generated MessagePack resolver that includes the [MessagePackObject] type.
The generated resolver contains a formatter entry for the closed generic value type member (e.g., Item<int>), so the member is covered by the resolver.

plants.description: The location guard around the analyzer reporter is dropped, so diagnostics whose location is not part of the compilation being analyzed (metadata symbols have no source location) are now reported and the analyzer driver throws AD0001.

This Diagnostic.Create is evaluated unconditionally (its result is stored in a local before the reporter is consulted), so indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] throws IndexOutOfRangeException during the generator run as well, yielding CS8785 and no resolver.

The null-safe GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper is bypassed and DeclaringSyntaxReferences is indexed directly, so a member whose type comes from metadata (no syntax) throws IndexOutOfRangeException in the analyzer and produces AD0001.
Explicit delegate creation instead of a lambda conversion; identical behaviour.
Renames the helper's parameter from property to symbol (and its doc tag); no behavioural change.
Renames the local callback parameter report to reportAction; no behavioural change.

Only the IsInSource half of the guard is kept; the ContainsSyntaxTree check is gone, so a symbol that originates from another compilation (project reference) still has syntax references in that compilation's trees and the analyzer now reports a location outside the current compilation, which the driver rejects with AD0001.

The reporter is no longer null when running inside the source generator, so the generator now invokes the callback and dereferences the (null) analyzer reporter for any in-source diagnostic, aborting the generator with CS8785.
The null-returning location helper is replaced by First(), which throws InvalidOperationException for members declared in metadata; the analyzer no longer completes cleanly and emits AD0001.

Using the null-forgiving operator instead of the null-conditional removes the tolerance for metadata members; the resulting NullReferenceException aborts the generator, so the compiling assembly gets no generated resolver at all.

findings.message: The reportDiagnostic wrapper only checks diagnostic.Location.IsInSource instead of calling ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (lines 1450-1456), leaving ReportIfLocatedInCompilation unused. When a referenced project is supplied as a CompilationReference (such as in IDE project-to-project references), diagnostic.Location.IsInSource is true for syntax trees belonging to the referenced compilation, so reportAnalyzerDiagnostic will still be invoked with a location outside this.compilation, causing Roslyn to throw an ArgumentException (AD0001).

findings.message: `reportAnalyzerDiagnostic` is typed as nullable `Action<Diagnostic>?` and callers rely on `this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(...)` to skip reporting when it is null (e.g., during source generation). Wrapping it unconditionally in `diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic!, diagnostic)` makes `this.reportDiagnostic` always non-null; if `reportAnalyzerDiagnostic` is `null` and a diagnostic has a location in the current compilation, `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` (line 1448) invokes `report(diagnostic)` on `null` and throws `NullReferenceException`.

`RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync` sets `TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck` and only checks `Assert.Contains(expectedResolverHintName, hintNames)`, so the tests never verify that the generated resolver actually includes the `[MessagePackObject]` type or a formatter entry for the closed generic value type member.

For source properties, GetSyntax().GetLocation() also widens the diagnostic location from the identifier to the full property declaration.

points.reason: The change replaces direct DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing in TypeCollector with null-safe location helpers and adds generator tests verifying no CS8785 or warning-level diagnostics are emitted for closed generic structs and record structs from metadata.

TypeCollector safely obtains null locations for metadata members, filters out diagnostics not located in the analyzed compilation via ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, and is verified by analyzer tests against metadata references.

The added test asserts only that the resolver hint name is generated while skipping generated-source verification, and no resolver-emission code is shown in the diff to confirm the [MessagePackObject] type is included in the resolver.

Neither the diff in TypeCollector nor the assertions in GenericsFormatterTests show the contents of the generated resolver or how closed generic value types from referenced assemblies are registered as formatter entries.
